back: Renewable: replaced naturally (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, tidal, biomass). Non-renewable: finite (coal, oil, gas, uranium).
Reliable access to enough energy at an affordable price, now and in future.
The largest proven reserves are in the Middle East, with others in Venezuela, Canada, Russia and Nigeria.
Kazakhstan is the largest producer, followed by Canada, Namibia and Australia.
Very large in the United States, Russia, Australia, China and India; Zimbabwe's coal is at Hwange.
Wind and solar output varies with weather, so storage, back-up and grid links are needed.
Exporters gain income but risk dependence; importers face price and supply risks and diversify.
Wood, charcoal and dung are cheap and local but cause indoor smoke, deforestation and time spent collecting.
Demand is rising, especially in Asia; fossil fuels supply roughly four-fifths; solar and wind are growing fastest.
